$metadata.$description: Figma Variables sync format (Tokens Studio for Figma). Import through a Variables-compatible plugin, or through the Tokens Studio desktop/CLI sync. Token sets map to Figma Variable collections: 'global' holds the palette ramps and the numeric scales and is the only set a designer should alias FROM; 'semantic-light' and 'semantic-dark' are the two theme modes of the same collection, so switching a Figma frame's mode switches every aliased colour in it exactly as data-theme does on the web. The remaining sets are documentation-facing and are imported as their own collections. VALUES ARE SYNCED from the token JSON files under tokens/ by `python3 tools/build_exports.py --figma`, which rewrites every colour and number from source and leaves everything else alone; `python3 tools/validate_tokens.py` fails the build if the two disagree. Do not hand-edit a value: it will be overwritten, and until it is, it exists only in Figma, which is how a design file and a shipped page come to disagree. The set structure and the prose ARE maintained here, because they are written for a reader in Figma and are not derivable from the source. An alias such as {global.color.navy.900} is load-bearing and the sync deliberately preserves it: replaced with a literal, the variable stops responding to a mode switch.

$themes.name: Light
$themes.$description: The default theme. Enables every token in semantic-light and disables semantic-dark.

$themes.name: Dark
$themes.$description: The navy theme. Enables semantic-dark in place of semantic-light. A frame set to this mode must not contain any direct reference to a global palette colour: palette references do not change with the mode, which is exactly the defect the semantic tier exists to prevent.

global.$description: Palette ramps and numeric scales. Theme-independent: navy-900 is the same colour in both modes. Do not apply a token from this set directly to a layer in a design file. Apply the semantic equivalent, so the layer responds to a mode change. The only legitimate direct uses are a logo lockup, a chart series and a printed artefact, all of which need a fixed value.

200.$description: Secondary text on a navy surface — 11.06:1 against navy-900.

300.$description: Muted text on a navy surface — 7.57:1.

700.$description: Default border and chart gridline on navy — 1.43:1.

800.$description: Raised surface on the dark theme.

950.$description: Sunken surface on the dark theme.

500.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — gold. 6.98:1 on navy (text-safe on dark). 2.20:1 on ivory and 2.42:1 on white — NEVER text on a light surface.

600.$description: 2.99:1 on ivory. Icons and borders at the 3:1 boundary; not text.

700.$description: Gold for TEXT on a light surface — 4.93:1 on ivory, 5.42:1 on white.

100.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — ivory. Default light-theme page surface.

300.$description: Default border and chart gridline on the light theme — 1.21:1.

200.$description: Selection highlight. Navy-900 on it is 10.03:1.

300.$description: Link colour on a raised dark surface — 5.70:1 against navy-800.

400.$description: Link and focus on the dark PAGE surface — 4.80:1. Drops to 4.14:1 on navy-800, so use accent-300 inside a card.

500.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — accent. 4.10:1 on ivory, 4.50:1 on white: a focus ring, icon or border, not body text on a light surface.

600.$description: Link text on the light theme — 6.10:1 on ivory, 6.70:1 on white.

400.$description: Disabled and placeholder text — 1.86:1 on ivory. Exempt under WCAG 1.4.3 as an inactive component; never for content a user must read.

500.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — neutral. Light-theme form-control outline at 3.35:1 on ivory.

700.$description: Muted body text on the light theme — 5.97:1.

white.$description: Card and raised surface on the light theme, and the Easter season surface. Not a page surface anywhere else: ivory is the page.

scrim-light.$description: Modal scrim on the light theme — 80% navy-900.

scrim-dark.$description: Modal scrim on the dark theme — deeper than navy-950 so a dialog separates from a dark page.

spacing.$description: 4pt base scale, in px. Figma Variables are floats and carry no unit, so these are numbers: a spacing variable is understood to be pixels.

4.$description: THE DEFAULT. Card padding, stacked gaps, mobile page gutter.

radius.$description: Close to square by design. Inner-radius rule: an element inside a rounded container with padding between them takes max(0, outer - padding).

sm.$description: THE DEFAULT for a control: button, input, select, checkbox.

lg.$description: Card, dialog, modal. The largest structural radius.

medium.$description: The focus ring. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 requires a 2 CSS pixel thick perimeter, so 1px fails regardless of contrast.

icon.$description: Icon sizes and the stroke weight each size needs. Stroke weight is NOT proportional to size: a 1.5px stroke scaled to 16px renders at 1px, lands between device pixels and antialiases into a grey blur.

primary.$description: Minimum height and width for any primary control.

floor.$description: Absolute AA floor per WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8. Reached only by an inline icon inside a link whose whole line box is the target.

semantic-light.$description: Light-theme roles. Every token here aliases a global palette value, so changing a ramp step changes the theme. Page surface is ivory-100; cards are white so they read as raised from a value step alone, without a shadow.

raised.$description: 1.10:1 against page — separation comes from the value step plus the elevation, not from a border.

link.$description: 6.10:1 on page, 6.70:1 on raised. Links are also underlined — colour is never the only signal.

link-raised.$description: Identical to link on this theme, because ivory-100 and white are only 1.10:1 apart. The token exists so both themes expose the same shape.

link-visited.$description: 8.33:1 on page, 9.16:1 on raised. Distinct from link in hue AND lightness so the distinction survives deuteranopia.

brand.$description: Gold AS TEXT on a light surface — 4.93:1. Never substitute gold-500.

on-gold.$description: 6.98:1 on a gold-500 fill. White on gold is 2.42:1 and fails.

input.$description: 3.35:1 on page, 3.68:1 on raised — clears the 3:1 non-text requirement.

focus.$description: 4.10:1 on page, 4.50:1 on raised — above the 3:1 focus-appearance minimum.

success-tint.$description: Banner fill. Navy-900 text on it is 14.43:1.

warning.$description: 4.92:1. Darkened from the obvious amber, which sits near 3.8:1 and fails body text.

semantic-dark.$description: Dark-theme roles. Two differ from a naive inversion of the light theme, both because of a measured contrast result. text.brand is gold-500 rather than gold-700: on navy the brand gold is already text-safe at 6.98:1, so the darker substitute would be a needless loss of brand presence. text.link-raised is accent-300 rather than accent-400: accent-400 measures 4.80:1 on navy-900 but only 4.14:1 on navy-800, so a link inside a dark card fails AA unless it steps up.

raised.$description: 1.16:1 against page — the whole of the elevation signal available at this depth, which is why the dark theme also uses a hairline top edge.

muted.$description: 7.57:1 on page, 6.55:1 on raised — AAA on both.

link.$description: 4.80:1 on page. On raised it is 4.14:1 and fails — use link-raised inside a card.

link-raised.$description: 5.70:1 on raised. THIS is the token to use for a link inside a dark card.

input.$description: 4.50:1 on page, 3.89:1 on raised — clears 3:1 on both.

focus.$description: 4.80:1 on page, 4.14:1 on raised. A focus indicator needs 3:1, so both pass.

success-tint.$description: 1.26:1 against page; its own foreground is 7.22:1.

church-context.$description: Church-context pairs: the roles a page ABOUT a context needs. Applied per page, never per component — two adjacent components in different contexts on one page is not a design. These are fixed rather than mode-aware: a context panel is a coloured block sitting ON the page, not a recolouring OF the page.

text.$description: 17.04:1 — the highest text contrast in the system, deliberate for an audience that is often elderly and often distressed.

accent.$description: Links stay in the navy family: a bright interactive colour on a funeral page reads as commerce.

surface.$description: Pale for legibility in direct daylight, which is where a graveside phone is used.

accent.$description: 6.98:1 — gold is text-safe on navy, which is why the ceremonial register is dark.

liturgical-season.$description: Additive themes layered over the core identity. A season changes the ceremonial surface, its soft companion and one accent; navy, gold, ivory and the interactive accent are untouched. Seasons are date- and rite-dependent and are resolved by the consuming application from its own calendar — nothing here encodes a date range, because the start of Lent moves every year and the Eastern calendars differ by weeks. During the Paschal Triduum no season applies.

surface-soft.$description: 1.11:1 against the ivory page; navy text on it 13.87:1.

accent.$description: 4.64:1 on violet — gold is the Advent candle, so this is liturgically correct as well as accessible.

accent-rose.$description: Gaudete Sunday. 5.13:1 on ivory, 4.63:1 on the soft surface, but only 1.99:1 on the violet — never text or iconography on violet.

text-muted-on-surface.$description: 8.44:1. Warm rather than cool, so a muted line does not read as an error.

candle.$description: The Advent wreath's four candles in the order they are lit: three violet and one rose. The one place in the system where a colour SEQUENCE carries liturgical meaning, so the numbers are the content and reordering them is a doctrinal error rather than a tidy-up.

3.$description: Gaudete Sunday — the rose candle is lit third.

surface.$description: Penitence. A deeper, more desaturated violet than Advent: Advent violet anticipates, Lent violet mourns. Ivory text 11.46:1.

surface-soft.$description: Warm unbleached-linen grey, not a violet wash — Lent strips colour rather than adding it.

accent.$description: Ash. 5.37:1 on ivory, 4.96:1 on the soft surface — text-safe on both. White on an ash fill is 5.90:1. Only 2.13:1 against the violet surface, so ash is a foreground on a light ground; use the rule token inside the dark surface.

accent-rose.$description: Laetare Sunday — the same rose as Advent, so the two rose days read as one gesture.

gold-permitted.$description: Suppressed through most of Lent, returning at Laetare and in the Triduum. 5.21:1 on the Lent surface.

surface.$description: The only season whose surface is white, which is the whole point: after six weeks of violet the page should feel like it has opened a window. Navy text 16.90:1.

surface-soft.$description: Candle-white with a breath of warmth, so a card on a white Easter page still separates.

accent.$description: DECORATION ONLY on this surface — 2.42:1 against white. For the paschal candle glyph, rules, initials and large display type on a navy band.

accent-text.$description: Gold that may carry meaning as text on an Easter surface — 5.42:1 on white, 5.24:1 on the soft surface.

pentecost.$description: Red for Pentecost, which closes the season, and for feasts of martyrs and apostles. 7.80:1 against white, in both directions. Inside Easter rather than a fifth theme, because it is a single day.

surface.$description: Growth, and the default for content not tied to a season — which is most content most of the year. Ivory text 7.21:1.

surface-soft.$description: 1.07:1 against the ivory page. Navy text on it 14.43:1, and the season green itself 6.76:1.

accent.$description: 3.28:1 on green: clears the 3:1 non-text threshold for an icon, a rule or a 24px display heading, and FAILS the 4.5:1 text threshold. That distinction is the one a reviewer is most likely to blur.

accent-text.$description: Gold as text on the Ordinary surface — 5.25:1. Only 1.29:1 on the soft surface, so on a pale green wash use semantic light text.brand instead.

chart.$description: Categorical series, ordered as a luminance staircase so consecutive series alternate dark and light. Two properties hold by construction and are re-verified by tools/contrast_check.py: every series clears 3:1 against its surface (WCAG 1.4.11), and consecutive series are separated by at least 2.28:1 so a stacked bar stays legible in greyscale and under colour-vision deficiency. Hue alone never carries meaning: label series directly or ship a monochrome alternative, per WCAG 1.4.1. Eight series maximum.

light.$description: On the ivory page surface. Worst on-surface contrast 3.06:1; worst consecutive separation 2.28:1.

7.$description: Sienna — 7.31:1, separated from 6 by 2.28:1, the tightest pair.

grid.$description: 1.21:1. Deliberately below 3:1: a gridline is scaffolding and must not compete with the data.

dark.$description: On the navy page surface. Inverted staircase. Worst on-surface contrast 3.59:1; worst consecutive separation 2.47:1.

typography.$description: Type scale in px, converted from the rem values in tokens/typography.json at a 16px root. Figma Variables are unitless floats, so the conversion is lossy in one specific way that matters: a designer who scales a Figma frame does not scale these values, whereas a browser that honours a larger default font size does. A Figma comp at 16px body is therefore a statement about the design at one user setting, not about the shipped product. Sizes below are the design-time truth; the rem values are the runtime truth.

display.$description: Headings, heroes, pull quotes, anything above 24px. Latin, Latin Extended and Vietnamese coverage.

display-cyrillic.$description: Russian display. Fraunces does not declare Cyrillic coverage, so a Russian heading set in Fraunces falls back glyph by glyph and renders as two typefaces in one line. Verify with tools/cyrillic_check.py against the actual binaries before a release.

ui.$description: Body copy, labels, buttons, tables, forms, navigation. Covers Latin, Latin Extended and Cyrillic, so one family serves lt, en and ru.

mono.$description: Design-time stand-in for the platform monospace stack. The web ships a platform stack (ui-monospace, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, Liberation Mono) and no webfont, because a monospace webfont costs 40-90KB for text almost no visitor reads. Do not export this value to code.

caption.$description: THE MINIMUM TEXT SIZE in the system.

button-lg.$description: One pixel above body-md, deliberately: a button label at exactly body size disappears into surrounding prose.

line-height.$description: In px, computed as the unitless multiplier times the role's own size. tokens/typography.json holds the unitless multiplier, which is the value that ships.

letter-spacing.$description: In px, computed as the em value times the role's own size. Design tools express tracking in px or %; the web expresses it in em, and em is correct because it scales with the size.

overline.$description: 0.1em at 12px. The floor for legible uppercase; below about 0.08em the words close into a grey bar.

measure.$description: Line length. The web tokens express measure in `ch`, which is the advance width of the '0' glyph in the resolved font and therefore cannot be converted to a fixed pixel value without measuring the actual font file — any px number written here would be an approximation presented as a fact. The one authoritative pixel value is the prose container width, which is what a Figma frame should actually be built at: 720px puts body-lg at 18px near the 66ch optimum for Inter. Set a text layer's width to container-prose and let the type fill it; do not compute a ch-to-px figure.

layout.$description: Breakpoints, gutters and containers. Figma frames are built at these widths; the media queries in build/css/reset.css use the same numbers literally, because a CSS custom property cannot appear in a media query condition. tools/validate_tokens.py fails the build when the three copies disagree.

lg.$description: The primary target for a parish dashboard: a ten-year-old 1366x768 machine with the browser not maximised lands here.

minimum-viewport.$description: The narrowest width that must render without horizontal scrolling. A failure here is a WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow failure.

motion.$description: Durations in milliseconds. Figma Smart Animate consumes these as numbers. No easing curve here overshoots: a spring is a simulator-sickness trigger and is rejected outright rather than merely disabled under reduced motion, so no design can come to depend on one. Under prefers-reduced-motion every duration collapses to 1ms — not 0ms, because a zero-length CSS transition never fires transitionend and leaves a component stuck in its pre-transition state.

fast.$description: Hover states, focus ring appearance, tooltip fade-in. The most-used duration.

base.$description: THE DEFAULT. If a transition has no obvious duration, it is 200ms.

ceremonial.$description: The longest permitted, reserved for the hero reveal at first paint. Never for a state change, never repeated, never on anything the user is waiting on.

easing.$description: Cubic-bezier control points, as strings. Figma's own easing presets do not map onto these exactly, so a prototype that must match the shipped curve needs a custom bezier entered by hand.

standard.$description: The default. A state change that neither enters nor leaves the viewport.

emphasized.$description: Gravity rather than speed: the hero reveal and ceremonial motion.

decelerate.$description: Anything ARRIVING. An arriving object that starts slowly looks reluctant.

accelerate.$description: Anything LEAVING. An exiting object that decelerates looks like it changed its mind.

linear.$description: Elapsed-time indicators only. Easing a progress bar misrepresents the remaining time.
